common_name: Florida Speckled Lima Bean (Heat-Tolerant Southern Pole Lima)

planting.note: Direct sow after soil is thoroughly warm, above 65°F; this Southern heirloom pole lima tolerates the heat and humidity of a Gulf Coast summer better than many Northern-bred lima varieties.

directions: Direct sow an inch deep in warm, fertile soil in full sun once soil temperatures stay reliably above 65°F, providing a trellis or pole for the climbing vine. Florida Speckled is a Southern heirloom pole lima bean grown for its handsome maroon-and-white speckled seeds and, more importantly, for genuine heat tolerance that lets it set pods reliably through the hot, humid conditions of a Deep South summer that cause many lima varieties to drop blossoms and stop producing. The vigorous vine climbs readily and produces well over an extended season once established. Harvest pods at the green shell stage for the classic buttery lima flavor, or allow pods to dry fully on the vine for a dry bean harvest that stores well through winter.

common_name: Big Mama Lima Bean (Large-Podded Creamy Pole Lima)

planting.note: Direct sow after soil is thoroughly warm, above 65°F, providing a sturdy trellis for the vigorous climbing vine.

directions: Direct sow an inch deep in warm, fertile soil in full sun once soil temperatures stay reliably above 65°F, providing a sturdy trellis for the climbing vine. Big Mama is a pole lima bean bred for large, broad, flat pods carrying big, creamy-textured seeds, giving a substantial harvest per pod compared to smaller-seeded lima types and making shelling more efficient for a given volume of beans. The rich, buttery flavor and dense, satisfying texture have made it a popular choice for Southern home gardeners who want generously sized lima beans for classic Southern succotash, butter bean dishes, and freezing for winter use. Harvest pods at the green shell stage once well filled for the best flavor and texture, and pick regularly to keep the productive vine setting new pods through the season.

planting.note: Direct sow after soil is thoroughly warm, above 65°F; the compact bush habit needs no trellis, unlike pole-type limas.

directions: Direct sow an inch deep in warm, fertile soil in full sun once soil temperatures stay reliably above 65°F. Dixie Butterpea is a compact bush-type lima bean, sparing gardeners the trellising that pole lima varieties require while still delivering the classic small, mild-flavored, buttery-textured seeds Southern cooks know as butterpeas or butter beans. The bush habit concentrates its harvest into a shorter window than pole types, making it convenient for a single large batch of shelling and canning or freezing, and the plant's heat tolerance suits it well to Southern growing conditions. Harvest pods at the green shell stage once well filled for classic butterpea flavor, and succession sow every few weeks through summer for a more continuous supply if desired.

common_name: Thorogreen Lima Bean (Green-Seeded Bush Baby Lima)

planting.note: Direct sow after soil is thoroughly warm, above 65°F; a compact bush type needing no trellis.

directions: Direct sow an inch deep in warm, fertile soil in full sun once soil temperatures stay reliably above 65°F. Thorogreen is a bush-type baby lima bean prized for seeds that stay a pale green color even after cooking, rather than the more common cream or white of most lima beans, giving finished dishes an appealingly fresh, vibrant appearance. The compact plant sets pods over a relatively short, concentrated window typical of bush lima types, making it convenient for a single main harvest for canning or freezing, and the small, tender seeds cook quickly with a mild, sweet flavor. Harvest pods at the green shell stage once well filled, and pick promptly once pods mature, since lima pods left too long on the plant can toughen.
